backlog.spec: After the first random restart, keep the best (centers, radii) found so far. For the remaining time, repeatedly copy the best solution, add Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.03) to all centers, reset radii to a small value, re-run the SLSQP local solve, repair, and accept the new packing only if its radius sum is larger. Keep the random-restart code path as a fallback for the first 20 percent of the time budget.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from incumbent best

backlog.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the constraint vector with respect to the 3n variables (centers and radii). For each pair row the derivative w.r.t. the two centers is the unit vector between them and w.r.t. the two radii is -1; boundary rows are simple +-1 entries. Build the Jacobian with numpy indexing rather than finite differences. This speeds each SLSQP iteration and lets more restarts fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Supply a jac for the objective -sum(r) to SLSQP, which is a constant vector of zeros for centers and minus ones for radii. Combined with the constraint Jacobian this removes finite-difference gradient evaluation entirely and reduces wall time per local solve.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for objective

backlog.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, include only pairs whose centers are closer than a threshold (for example the sum of radii plus 0.15) at the start of each local solve. Rebuild the active pair list after each SLSQP call and rerun once if any pair that was excluded now overlaps. This shrinks the constraint vector and makes each SLSQP iteration cheaper for n = 26.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-only pair constraints

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and add ftol set to 1e-12 so that SLSQP runs to convergence rather than stopping early. Check the result's success flag and count restarts that did not converge separately so the time budget is used on converged local optima.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so that the restart loop uses about 27 of the 30 CPU seconds, leaving margin below the 45 s void threshold. Also measure the duration of the last solve and stop starting a new restart if the predicted finish would exceed 0.9 of the budget.
backlog.title: Use more of the time budget

backlog.spec: Replace the hard inequality constraints in the first phase with a quadratic penalty on overlaps and boundary violations, solved with L-BFGS-B over the 3n variables. Multiply the penalty weight by 10 over several stages (for example 1e2 up to 1e7) and warm-start each stage from the previous one. Finish with a short SLSQP run on the exact constraints to polish the result.
backlog.title: Penalty method with increasing weight

backlog.spec: After the centers are fixed by the optimizer, compute the best radii with a linear program: maximize sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= boundary distance of center i. Solve it with scipy.optimize.linprog using the highs method. This replaces the greedy repair with an exact radius assignment for the given centers and keeps the packing valid by construction, apart from a tiny safety margin.
backlog.title: Exact radius LP given centers

backlog.spec: Before returning, multiply all radii by (1 - 1e-9) and subtract a 1e-12 absolute margin so that floating point round-off in SLSQP output cannot produce an overlap beyond the harness tolerance of 1e-10. Verify the final packing with a vectorised overlap check and fall back to the repaired version if the check fails.
backlog.title: Shrink margin for exact validity

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random centers, seed each restart from a hexagonal-style grid of 26 points inside [0.1, 0.9] squared, chosen by taking a random row count and column count with the right capacity, then remove or add points at random to hit exactly n and add uniform jitter of about 0.02. Initial radii are set to half the nearest-neighbour distance. Restarts still use the seed rng.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-grid initialisation with jitter

backlog.spec: Set each initial radius to 0.5 times the distance to its nearest neighbouring center, capped by the boundary distance, instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS of 0.05. This gives SLSQP a feasible or nearly feasible starting point and reduces the number of iterations spent recovering from initial overlap.
backlog.title: Random initial radii from neighbour distances

backlog.spec: Generate initial centers by sequential random sampling: draw candidate points uniformly in the square and accept each one only if it is at least 0.12 from all accepted centers, retrying up to 200 times per point and relaxing the threshold if needed. This produces well spread starts that fit the packing structure better than independent uniform draws.
backlog.title: Uniform random point cloud with rejection

backlog.spec: As a perturbation move in the search loop, take the current best packing, delete the circle with the smallest radius, and reinsert it at a random location inside the square with radius zero. Run the local SLSQP solve on the resulting configuration and keep it if the sum improves. This targets the rattler circles that carry little radius and gives the search a discrete move beyond Gaussian noise.
backlog.title: Remove and reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Perturb the best packing by swapping the positions of two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.05, then re-solve locally with SLSQP. Accept if the radius sum improves. Use a fixed number of swap attempts per restart chosen from the seeded rng. Swapping sizes lets the structure reorganise without a full restart.
backlog.title: Swap moves between large and small circles

backlog.spec: In the basin hopping loop, accept a worse local optimum with probability exp(-(old_sum - new_sum)/T) where T starts at 0.01 and decays geometrically to 1e-4 over the time budget. Keep track of the best packing seen and return that one, not the current state. Use the seeded rng for all acceptance draws.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing acceptance on local optima

backlog.spec: Within basin hopping, start with a Gaussian centre-noise sigma of 0.05 and multiply it by 0.9 after each rejected move and by 1.1 after each accepted move, clipped to the range [0.005, 0.1]. This lets the search take large jumps when stuck and small refinements when near a good optimum.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation strength

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the top 5 distinct packings by radius sum. Each new iteration either starts fresh (probability 0.3) or picks a random elite packing and perturbs it (probability 0.7). Replace the worst elite when a new packing beats it and differs by a sum gap of at least 1e-6. Return the best elite at the end.
backlog.title: Multi-start with elite pool

backlog.spec: For some restarts, generate initial centers with a mirror symmetry about the vertical or horizontal axis of the square, or a 90 degree rotational symmetry, by sampling half or a quarter of the points and reflecting or rotating them. Symmetric starts often lead to good packings of square-like problems. Mix symmetric and asymmetric starts with equal probability chosen from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Symmetric initial configurations

backlog.spec: Run the first SLSQP solve with a modified objective that weights radii by a random factor between 0.8 and 1.2 per circle, then run a second solve with the true unweighted objective starting from its result. The random weights break symmetry in different ways per seed and can move the search to better basins.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective warm-up

backlog.spec: First solve for centers only with all radii fixed to a common value chosen so that the packing is near feasible (for example 0.075), minimising the overlap penalty with SLSQP. Then release the radii and run the full SLSQP on centers and radii. The two-stage approach gives a sensible layout before radii are optimised, which can avoid poor local optima.
backlog.title: Two-stage solve with fixed radii first

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of gradient descent on the energy sum of squared pair overlaps plus boundary violations with the radii fixed at the initial value. This relaxes the random start toward a non-overlapping arrangement so that SLSQP begins from a nearly feasible point. Use a fixed step size of 0.01 and stop when the energy drops below 1e-8.
backlog.title: Overlap-penalty gradient descent pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Pre-relax initial centers with a repulsive force field: for each pair apply a force proportional to the inverse square of distance pushing them apart, and a wall repulsion, iterating about 200 times with a damping factor of 0.9. Use the resulting spread as the starting centers for SLSQP. This gives an even spacing and is cheap to compute with numpy broadcasting.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style repulsion relaxation

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise repair in _repair with a loop that, for each overlapping pair, shrinks both radii by the same fraction needed to remove the overlap, and repeats over all pairs until none overlaps by more than 1e-12 or 200 sweeps have run. Keep the boundary clipping first. This keeps more radius sum than shrinking only the single worst pair per step.
backlog.title: Vectorised repair with neighbour-aware scaling

backlog.spec: Before the pairwise repair, clip each center to the square [r_i, 1 - r_i] for its current radius and reduce any radius that exceeds the distance to a wall. Then run the existing repair. This ordering keeps the boundary constraints tight and reduces the amount of radius lost in the pairwise step.
backlog.title: Shrink-to-boundary before repair

backlog.spec: Rank each restart by the radius sum obtained after the exact radius LP from the linprog idea, not by the repaired SLSQP output, so that the choice of best restart reflects the true valid packing value. Keep only the best such packing across restarts.
backlog.title: Compute best by total radius after exact LP polish

backlog.spec: Change INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.02 so that initial centers can start close to the boundary and the search covers the whole square, including corners where many circles of different sizes sit. Keep the rest of the initialisation unchanged. The boundary constraints in SLSQP still enforce validity.
backlog.title: Lower INIT_LOW margin

backlog.spec: Derive a separate seeded rng for each restart from the pair (seed, restart index) using numpy SeedSequence spawn, so that restarts are reproducible and independent of how many restarts fit in the time budget. This makes the three-seed mean less noisy when comparing variants, though it does not change expected quality.
backlog.title: Fixed random seed per restart index

backlog.spec: Each outer iteration, generate a batch of 8 perturbed copies of the current best packing with different noise levels from the set {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1}, solve all eight locally with SLSQP, and adopt the best one if it improves on the current best. This batch hill-climb spends time evenly across perturbation scales within one loop.
backlog.title: Parallel-style batch of perturbed starts

backlog.spec: After a first SLSQP solve, identify pairs whose slack (distance minus radii sum) is larger than 0.2 and drop their constraints from a second, cheaper SLSQP solve that refines the solution. Re-add any dropped pair that becomes violated in the refined result and resolve once more. This keeps the final precision while cutting the constraint count.
backlog.title: Fewer constraints by dropping inactive pairs

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty term 1e-4 times the sum of squared differences between each radius and the mean radius to the SLSQP objective. This encourages a more even set of radii, which sometimes lets the optimiser escape configurations dominated by a few large circles and find a higher total. Remove the penalty in a final unregularised SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Mild L2 regularisation on radii spread

backlog.spec: In solve, each restart first optimises a packing of n+1 circles with the existing _solve_once and _repair. Remove the circle with the smallest radius, then re-run _solve_once for n circles seeded from the remaining centres and radii (x0 built from them instead of random centres) with the same SLSQP call. Keep the usual best-by-sum comparison and the repair step. The n+1 pass gives a different basin, and the deletion gives a warm start for the n-circle problem. Keep the change to about 15 lines.
backlog.title: Over-provision then delete the smallest

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the best 4 repaired packings found so far, with their seeds and sums. For each new restart with probability 0.5, pick two elites A and B. Make a child by taking the circles of A whose centres have x < a random cut value c, and the circles of B with x >= c. If the count is not n, add or drop circles with the largest or smallest x near the cut to reach n. Start SLSQP from the child centres with radii 0.05, then repair. Otherwise use a fresh random start. Replace the worst elite when the child is better.
backlog.title: Crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed restart loop with a successive-halving schedule. Draw 16 random starts and run SLSQP on each with MAX_ITER=30. Keep the best 4 by repaired sum and rerun them with MAX_ITER=200 from their current x. Keep the best 1 of those and run it to MAX_ITER=400. Repeat the whole cycle while the CPU time budget (TIME_FRACTION * time_limit) lasts, and always return the best repaired packing seen. Track time with time.process_time as now.
backlog.title: Successive halving over random starts

backlog.spec: Replace the rejection-sampled uniform initial centres in _solve_once with a Halton sequence in base 2 and 3 for the x and y coordinates. Use a random offset per restart drawn from rng so that restarts differ. Shrink each point toward the centre by a random factor in [0.9, 1.0] to keep circles off the boundary before SLSQP. Keep the rest of _solve_once and _repair unchanged. Implement the Halton generator in about 8 lines of numpy using the radical inverse function.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, instead of starting every radius at INIT_RADIUS = 0.05, draw initial radii from a log-normal distribution rng.lognormal(mean=log(0.07), sigma=0.6, size=n), then clip them to [0.01, 0.2]. Strongly unequal starts often reach packings with a few large and many small circles, which is typical of good 26-circle solutions. Leave the centre initialisation and the SLSQP call unchanged. This is a one-line change to x0 plus the clip.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed initial radii

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in three stages instead of one. Each stage adds bounds to the variables: each centre coordinate may move at most delta from its value at the start of the stage, and each radius may move at most delta, with delta = 0.15, then 0.05, then 0.01. Pass these as the bounds argument of minimize, using (max(0, v-delta), min(1, v+delta)) for centre coordinates and (0, 0.5) for radii with the delta window applied. Start each stage from the previous stage's output and use MAX_ITER per stage. Then repair. This keeps SLSQP from jumping across basins and tends to converge more cleanly.
backlog.title: Trust-region SLSQP with per-stage move bounds

backlog.spec: After the first repaired packing of each restart, run a loop until the time limit. In each iteration choose a random centre point and remove the k=4 circles nearest to it. Reinsert them at random points inside a disk of radius 0.2 around the removed region, with radius 0.02. Run SLSQP on the whole packing for all n circles from this start with MAX_ITER=100, then repair. Accept the new packing if its radius sum is greater than or equal to the current one, and otherwise keep the current one. Return the best accepted packing.
backlog.title: Large neighbourhood destroy-and-repair

backlog.spec: After _repair, run a greedy growth pass. Visit the circles in a random order from rng. For each circle, set its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and at least the distance to every other circle minus that circle's neighbour radius, computed exactly from current centres and radii. Repeat the pass twice. The greedy pass only increases radii where room exists, and the result is checked by the same validity rule. Put it in a new function _grow(c, r, rng) called before the best comparison in solve.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth after repair

backlog.spec: For odd n, put one circle fixed at the centre (0.5, 0.5) and optimise (n-1)/2 free centres p_k and radii r_k. Their mirror images are at (1,1)-p_k with the same radii. Pass the free variables to SLSQP and build the full centre and radius arrays inside the constraint and objective functions. Add the same boundary and non-overlap constraints as before, with the mirror copies included. This reduces the variable count and searches a symmetric subspace, which is a different search from the current unconstrained one. Keep the random restart loop and repair unchanged. Use n-1 even as the guard and fall back to _solve_once for other n.
backlog.title: Enforce half-turn symmetry in SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add an upper bound on every radius that is raised across three SLSQP stages. Start with a cap of 0.06, and run SLSQP with MAX_ITER stage 1. Then raise the cap to 0.12 and then to 0.5, running SLSQP each time from the last output. Implement the cap through the bounds argument (0, cap) on the radii. The cap keeps early stages from fixing a few large circles in place and blocking packings that use many medium circles. Then repair as now.
backlog.title: Radius-cap continuation

backlog.spec: Replace the random uniform initial centres in _solve_once with a greedy largest-empty-circle construction. Place the first circle at a random point. For each next circle, sample about 2000 random candidate points in [0,1]^2 with the rng, compute each candidate's distance to the nearest existing centre and to the square boundary, and choose the candidate with the largest such clearance (with a little random jitter on the score to keep diversity). Use the chosen points as the start for the existing SLSQP call, with INIT_RADIUS set to the clearance at placement. Keep the restart loop, _repair and the best-of selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Largest-hole greedy construction

backlog.spec: In solve, keep a warm-start packing for n-1 circles from a short SLSQP run (for example 1/4 of the per-restart budget). Insert one new circle at the largest empty spot found by sampling candidate points, as in the largest-hole rule, and then run the full SLSQP on all n circles from this start. Alternate between the growth path and fresh random restarts, and keep the best result by sum of radii as now. The goal is to reach good basins by growing a packing rather than starting from scratch every time.
backlog.title: Grow from an (n-1)-circle optimum

backlog.spec: After the first 30 percent of the time budget, take the current best packing (centres and radii). Build its 8 images under the square's dihedral group: reflections and 90-degree rotations, using c -> 1 - c on the relevant coordinates and swapping x and y for the rotations. Run SLSQP on each image, plus a copy with small Gaussian jitter (sd 0.01) on the centres. Repair each result and keep the best by sum of radii. Use the remaining time for random restarts, as now. This tests whether symmetric variants of a good packing lie in nearby, better basins.
backlog.title: Dihedral symmetry restarts of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, first solve a restricted problem where all radii equal a single variable s: maximise s subject to the pair constraints dist >= 2s and the wall constraints c >= s, 1-c >= s, using SLSQP on the centres and s only. Use the resulting centres, with radii set to s, as the start for the existing full SLSQP that frees every radius. The equal-radius optimum is a strong starting structure for mixed-radius packings, and this step gives the free-radius solve a better start than uniform random centres with radius 0.05.
backlog.title: Equal-radius warm start then free radii

backlog.spec: After SLSQP returns a candidate (centres c, radii r), polish it with a log-barrier method. Maximise sum(r) + mu * sum(log g_k(c, r)) over the inequality slacks g_k (pair distances minus radius sums, wall clearances, and r >= 0), using scipy minimize with L-BFGS-B on the analytic gradient, or with a numerical gradient if simpler. Decrease mu geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-7 over about 8 stages, warm-starting each stage. Only accept the polished result if it is valid and has a larger sum of radii. Do not change the restart loop.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point final polish

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, identify the active constraints: pairs whose slack is below 1e-7 and wall or radius bounds that are tight. Form the square system of equations that sets these active constraints to zero, together with the stationarity conditions for the circles, if the system is square; otherwise use Gauss-Newton on the active set with least squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq. Take a few Newton steps to drive the active slacks to machine precision. Then run _repair with the existing shrink step and accept the result only if it improves the sum of radii. This removes the small residual slack left by SLSQP's stopping tolerance.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton KKT polish

backlog.spec: Change the initial placement in _solve_once so that the largest circles are placed first. Draw a random target radius profile (for example radii from a random Beta distribution scaled to sum around 2.6), place the four largest circles in the four corners with a random inset, then place the others by the largest-clearance rule, in decreasing order of target radius. Use the resulting centres as the start for the existing SLSQP and set the starting radii from the target profile. Keep _repair and the restart loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored large-first initialisation

backlog.spec: Rewrite the pair inequality in cons as squared form to remove the square root and its gradient singularity at zero distance: use (cx_i - cx_j)^2 + (cy_i - cy_j)^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 together with r_i + r_j >= 0, which is valid because the radii are nonnegative. Also pass a jac argument to SLSQP that computes the Jacobian of these constraints analytically with numpy, or leave it numerical if the analytic version is risky. Keep the initial centres and the repair step unchanged. This should speed up each SLSQP iteration and let more restarts fit in the same time.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, run SLSQP in stages with objective maximise sum(r_i^p) for p ramping from 0.5 to 1.0 over three stages (for example p = 0.5, 0.75, 1.0), passing the solution of each stage as the start of the next. Use the same constraints throughout. The power objective penalises unequal radii early, which steers the search away from degenerate configurations with a few large circles and many tiny ones, and the final stage optimises the true objective sum(r). Keep the repair and the restart loop as they are.
backlog.title: Power-law objective continuation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add a margin eps to every pair constraint, dist - (r_i + r_j) >= eps, and to every wall constraint. Start eps at 0.02, which lets SLSQP move freely through overlapping configurations, then run a sequence of SLSQP solves that decreases eps to 0.02, 0.01, 0.003, 0.0 and warm-starts each stage from the previous one. Final validity is still ensured by _repair, applied only at the end. The relaxed early stages allow circles to pass around one another and may reach better basins than solving the exact constrained problem from the start.
backlog.title: Margin-relaxation continuation

incumbent.description: Fix the dimension mismatch in `_solve_once` by reshaping the concatenated array to be 2D (or by flattening the centers) to ensure consistency with the solver's expectation of a 1D array.

memo:
Helped: only slot 5, a dimension-mismatch bug fix in _solve_once (-2.6299/-2.6328, mean -2.6313 over 2 runs, the incumbent). No new search idea has beaten it yet.

Did not help: L-BFGS-B penalty (slot 3, -2.6092) and Halton init (slot 17, -2.6226) were clearly worse. Remove-and-reinsert (slot 9, -2.6324), elite pool (slot 10, -2.6303), more restart time (slot 15, -2.6299), batch perturbation (slot 16, -2.6294), successive halving (slot 22, -2.6293), hex init (slot 23, -2.6300) and equal-radius warm start (slot 31, -2.6315) were within noise (sd about 0.0023), so none is proven.

Process: many slots were lost to patch failures (10 of the 21 slots listed in the previous notes) and to crashes. Crashes clustered around analytic Jacobians, LP repair and custom initialisations.

Next: copy SEARCH text exactly and keep edits small. Check shapes and syntax before submitting. Replicate the incumbent once to pin down its true mean. Then try basin-hopping from the best packing, with a gentler repair step.
